tagline: Redwoods first, then a river road climbing toward Oregon.
intro: From near Crescent City, US 199 enters Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park, climbs over a ridge, crosses the Smith River, and then climbs steadily beside the river and its Middle Fork, past Hiouchi and Gasquet. Near the summit the Middle Fork turns east and the highway follows Griffin Creek instead.

The first road out of Crescent City, in 1858, was laid in planks. In the 1880s Horace Gasquet added a corduroy toll road from Gasquet Flats to the state line near Oregon Mountain. The modern highway keeps the river company through much of the California stretch.

moments.title: Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park
moments.text: Named for Jedediah Smith, who passed through in 1826, the park keeps old-growth redwoods along the Smith River just after the highway leaves US 101.

moments.title: Gasquet
moments.text: Near where the North and Middle forks meet, the highway crosses the Smith on a bridge named in 1932 for Mary Adams Peacock, who carried the mail to Grants Pass.

moments.title: Collier Tunnel
moments.text: Since July 20, 1963, the highway has gone under Hazel View Summit at about 2,100 feet, and the old curving road over the top survives as Oregon Mountain Road.
